solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Give up short-lived thrill (4)

blocks.note: to quit a habit, as in to ___ smoking
a quick jolt of pleasure, as from a strong drink

annotation.surface: Someone resolving to quit a cheap habit that only ever gave a fleeting buzz.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one piece of advice, so the join between 'Give up' and 'short-lived thrill' is easy to miss.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: you kick a habit to give it up, and a drink with a kick gives a brief thrill.

entries.clue: Having trouble making runs in innings, want to be caught (5-5)

indicatorNotes.to be caught: a sound is caught by the ear, so what follows is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: in cricket a batsman's innings is called a knock
want = need, which sounds like KNEED

annotation.surface: A struggling batsman who can't score and would almost rather be caught out and walk off.
annotation.walkthrough: The cricket surface makes 'runs' look like scoring; in the definition it is running, which knock-kneed people find awkward. In cricket a 'knock' is an innings, and being 'caught' is a way of getting out.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone knock-kneed has knees that knock together, so running is awkward for them.

entries.clue: Toboggan run avoids a hilltop (5)

indicatorNotes.avoids: the run steers clear of the A, so the A is left out

blocks.note: the Cresta Run is the famous toboggan run at St Moritz

annotation.surface: A sledging course laid out so that it skirts round the top of a hill.
annotation.walkthrough: The Cresta Run is a toboggan track in St Moritz, Switzerland; drop its final A and the hilltop remains.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the highest ridge of a hill is its crest.

entries.clue: Started job, shifting beautiful little pieces (6,4)

indicatorNotes.shifting: the letters shift about into a new order

annotation.surface: A new employee beginning work on a shift, moving delicate ornaments around.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Started job, shifting' reads as someone starting a shift at work; 'shifting' is really rearranging the ten letters before it.
annotation.definitionFit: Objets d'art are small decorative items valued for their beauty.

entries.clue: Blessing moors in remote region of US (9)

blocks.note: to moor a boat is to dock it

annotation.surface: A benediction pronounced over wild moorland in some far-flung corner of America.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Moors' looks like a noun for heathland; here it is the verb, tying up a boat.
annotation.definitionFit: The boondocks is American slang for remote, rough country far from towns.

entries.clue: Came closer, not at first lugged (5)

indicatorNotes.not at first: the word's opening letter is not there

blocks.note: to come closer is to near

annotation.surface: Someone approaching while hauling something heavy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lugged' looks like carried with effort; here it is the adjective from 'lug', British slang for ear, so 'lugged' means having ears.
annotation.definitionFit: Lugs are ears, so lugged means eared, having ears.

entries.clue: I wouldn’t easily believe sort of tank that captures carbon (7)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is what a sceptic would say of themself, standing for the person

indicatorNotes.captures: the tank takes the C prisoner inside it

blocks.note: C is the chemical symbol for carbon

annotation.surface: Someone doubting a claim about a tank designed to trap carbon emissions.
annotation.walkthrough: SEPTIC wraps round C after its first letter: S-C-EPTIC.
annotation.definitionFit: A sceptic is someone slow to believe things, as the speaker describes themself.

entries.clue: Are away covering good area in the country (9)

indicatorNotes.covering: ARENT goes over and around the G

blocks.note: if people are away they aren't here: AREN'T

annotation.surface: A remark that some people are abroad, spread over a good stretch of countryside.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Are away' is the hard step: people who are away aren't here, so read it as the contraction. 'Area in' supplies its two pieces in the reverse of the order they appear.
annotation.definitionFit: The definition is a bare category; the answer is one example, the South American nation.

entries.clue: Nothing missed by card sharp (4)

indicatorNotes.missed by: the card goes without the O

blocks.note: a tarot is a fortune-telling card

annotation.surface: A card sharp so skilled that nothing gets past him.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Card sharp' reads as one phrase for a cheat at cards; split it and 'sharp' is the definition. O stands for nothing (zero).
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for taste: something sour and acidic is both.

entries.clue: Quietly turn canoe? (6)

blocks.note: eggs that turn or go bad are said to addle

annotation.surface: A murmured instruction to roll a canoe over.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Canoe' is a verb here, and the question mark admits that paddling is only one way of doing it. Milk turns and eggs addle: both mean go off.
annotation.definitionFit: To canoe is to paddle a small boat; the question mark flags the loose equivalence.

entries.clue: As theatre patron, agree: poor play (9)

indicatorNotes.play: the letters play about into a new order

annotation.surface: A theatregoer conceding that the evening's play was a poor one.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play' sits naturally in a theatre review as the show being judged; it is telling you to rearrange AGREE POOR.
annotation.definitionFit: An operagoer is a regular patron of the opera house, a kind of theatre.

entries.clue: Anxious always to lock silver away (5)

indicatorNotes.to lock: to lock something in is to hold it inside, as this word holds the silver
indicatorNotes.away: 'lock away' is the idiom for storing valuables out of sight, inside something

blocks.note: e'er, the poetic contraction of ever
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

annotation.surface: Someone who frets about security and always wants the family silver locked up.
annotation.walkthrough: E'ER is the poetic shortening of 'ever'; the silver goes in after its first letter: E-AG-ER.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, in the sense of keen: anxious to please means keen to please.

entries.clue: Insect with long legs: a thousand? We hear eighty was enough (7)

indicatorNotes.We hear: what follows is to be heard, not spelt

blocks.note: eighty did = eighty was enough, as in 'that did'

annotation.surface: Two naturalists debating whether a creature has a thousand legs or whether eighty would do.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A thousand' next to 'insect with long legs' suggests millipedes; it is only K. 'Did' means sufficed, as in 'that'll do'.
annotation.definitionFit: A katydid is a long-legged North American bush cricket.

entries.clue: Seeing what carbon may be used for (6)

annotation.definition2: what carbon may be used for

blocks.clueFragment: what carbon may be used for
blocks.note: radiocarbon measurement fixes the age of old organic material

annotation.surface: A science lesson on the uses of carbon, framed as looking at it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seeing' looks like eyesight; it is the romantic sense, going out with someone.
annotation.definitionFit: Seeing someone means dating them; carbon dating uses carbon to find an object's age.

entries.clue: Almost achieve concord in Kent town? Quite a lot (1,5,4)

indicatorNotes.Almost: the word stops one letter short

blocks.note: Deal is a seaside town in Kent

annotation.surface: Peace talks in a Kent town that nearly reach agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: Deal is a small town on the Kent coast in south-east England; 'in Deal' becomes AT DEAL.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase is a stock way of saying much or many.

entries.clue: Calculating how many people are eating celery? (6,9)

annotation.definition: Calculating how many people are eating celery?

blocks.note: the real definition: heavy arithmetic on data

blocks.clueFragment: how many people are eating celery?
blocks.note: the literal picture: a head-count of those munching noisily, since celery is the loudest thing to bite

annotation.walkthrough: Heavy calculation is number-crunching; taken literally it is the count of people crunching, and celery is the noisiest thing to crunch.
annotation.definitionFit: Number-crunching is doing large amounts of calculation.

entries.clue: Fools lower energy a bit in oppressive heat (9)

indicatorNotes.lower: the E is moved lower down the word
indicatorNotes.a bit: only a little way: one place

blocks.note: muggy weather is close and oppressive
E = energy, lifted out and set one place lower

annotation.surface: A grumble that idiots slow down only slightly in sweltering weather.
annotation.walkthrough: In MUGGINESS the E moves one place down the word: MUGGIN-E-SS becomes MUGGINS-E-S. 'Mugginses' is plural of muggins, British slang for a fool, often oneself.
annotation.definitionFit: A muggins is a gullible fool, so mugginses are fools.

entries.clue: Previously employed, northern counterpart is welcomed to general approval (9)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition is an adverbial phrase; the answer is its adjective, as in 'passed unopposed'

indicatorNotes.is welcomed: the counterpart is welcomed in, taken inside USED

blocks.note: oppo is British slang for one's opposite number or colleague

annotation.surface: A former employee's northern equivalent being welcomed back to applause.
annotation.walkthrough: The northern counterpart is welcomed inside what was previously employed. 'Oppo' is British slang for your opposite number or colleague.
annotation.definitionFit: A motion passed unopposed goes through with everyone's approval.

entries.clue: First school run requiring safe delivery of precious cargo? (3,3,5,4)

annotation.definition: First school run requiring safe delivery of precious cargo?

blocks.note: reads as parents' morning drive to a primary school; it is a running race at a first school's sports day

blocks.clueFragment: requiring safe delivery of precious cargo?
blocks.note: the cargo is an egg balanced on a spoon, which must reach the finish unbroken

annotation.walkthrough: The 'school run' sounds like parents driving children to school; it is a running race at a first (primary) school, and the precious cargo is an egg on a spoon. An egg and spoon race is a British sports-day staple.
annotation.definitionFit: In an egg and spoon race children run carrying an egg on a spoon without dropping it.

entries.clue: Greeting a Pole in outskirts of Nice (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' means placed inside, so the pole goes inside the outer letters

annotation.surface: Saying hello to a Polish visitor on the edge of Nice.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pole' is capitalised to suggest a person from Poland; it is a mast. The container splits NE at N|E.
annotation.definitionFit: Namaste is a respectful Indian greeting made with palms pressed together.

entries.clue: New weapon is limited (6)

annotation.surface: A complaint that the latest armament has only limited use.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is one short verdict on a weapon; 'limited' is the definition, as in a narrow range.
annotation.definitionFit: Narrow means limited in scope, as in a narrow outlook.

entries.clue: Got darker, turning round in the middle of sea (6)

indicatorNotes.turning round: MID turns round to face the other way

blocks.note: mid = in the middle, as in midway

annotation.surface: A sky clouding over as a ship turns about in mid-ocean.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In the middle of sea' reads as a position out at sea; split it, and 'in the middle' is one word's worth of letters while 'of' only joins it to the sea.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a light that dims grows darker.

entries.clue: Centre for recruits was lush, springing up (5)

indicatorNotes.springing up: in a down clue the word rises, reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: to tope is to drink heavily, as a lush does

annotation.surface: A training camp that used to be verdant, now bursting into growth.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lush' looks like green growth; it is a drunkard, so 'was lush' means drank to excess: toped.
annotation.definitionFit: A depot is a regimental headquarters where recruits are trained.

entries.clue: Soldier cherished defensive formation (7)

blocks.note: a pet project is a cherished one

annotation.surface: A trooper who loves a well-drilled defensive line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Formation' suggests troops drawn up in ranks; here it is a built structure, the protective wall on a rampart.
annotation.definitionFit: A parapet is a low protective wall, a defensive structure along a fortification.

entries.clue: Wonderful gymnast calling for silence (5)

annotation.definitionNote: the definition describes the answer as an interjection, 'Peace!'

blocks.note: PE, physical education, the gym lesson

annotation.surface: A brilliant gymnast asking the crowd to hush before a routine.
annotation.walkthrough: A wonderful gymnast is an ace at PE, so PE and ACE combine in that order.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Peace!' is an old command for quiet.

entries.clue: Priest’s flab being slimmed down (4)

indicatorNotes.slimmed down: the phrase is pared down to letters within it

blocks.note: strip FL from the front and ING from the end

annotation.surface: A cleric's paunch being trimmed by diet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a diet; trimming FL off the front and ING off the end of 'flab being' leaves the French priest.
annotation.definitionFit: An abbé is a French abbot or priest.

entries.clue: Foundation of building at first without modification (5)

indicatorNotes.at first: take only the first letter of building

annotation.surface: A builder's note that the house's foundations were laid just as planned.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Foundation of building' reads as one phrase; the definition stops at 'Foundation'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what something is built on is its base or foundation.

entries.clue: Secretary is to rank all the ministers (9)

annotation.surface: A government secretary tasked with grading every minister in the cabinet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ministers' suggests government; here they are clergy.
annotation.definitionFit: The pastorate is the body of pastors, ministers of religion, taken together.

entries.clue: Inconsistent dieters eat special eggs now? (10)

indicatorNotes.Inconsistent: the letters don't stay in a consistent order

annotation.surface: Wavering dieters giving in to chocolate eggs.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic hint: Eastertide is the season of chocolate eggs. 'Inconsistent' fits dieters who lapse, but it is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Eastertide is the Easter season, when special eggs are around.

entries.clue: Had an accident walking terrible hill (4)

blocks.note: tumbled, past tense of the verb for dropping to the ground
an archaic adjective for cruel or deadly, as in 'one ___ swoop'
northern English word for an upland hill, as walked in the Lake District

annotation.surface: A hiker who took a tumble on a nasty hill.
annotation.walkthrough: Three meanings of FELL: tumbled, cruel, and hill. 'Walking' hints at fell-walking, hiking over the hills of the Lake District.
annotation.definitionFit: Fell is past tense of fall, an archaic word for cruel, and a northern English hill.
